gap: No result ChatGPT got states what two of its five priced picks cost or do on a Mac. Xebec's $699 Tri-Screen 3 also needs Xebec's own Mac Adapter ($59 on sale, $99 list), which uses DisplayLink because Apple does not support MST. ViewSonic says on its US page for the $349.99 VG1457 that 'Dual-screen Extend mode is unavailable on macOS', so only one of its two screens extends.
standout_why: I read the three pages ChatGPT cited, plus its top uncited result. itechguides' 15-best page (cited) prices only five Amazon screens and three Lenovo listings. It gives no Mac display counts, does not cover Xebec or the VG1457, and says only that the laptop's display limit decides how many screens work. RTINGS' portable page (cited) showed no picks or prices in the fetched text. Macworld (cited) gives retailer prices for the Trio 3 Pro and says base M1/M2 Macs need free software for it, so the rivals already have part of the Mac story. Macworld does not cover Xebec, Aura or ViewSonic. The uncited itechguides 2025 page covers only the Xebec Snap, with no price and no adapter or DisplayLink note.
decides: This supports keeping the Trio 3 Pro as the pick for two added screens, and it changes the advice for Mac owners. ChatGPT priced the Trio 3 Pro at $423.99 (Walmart card) and $429.99. Through our link it is {after:mobile-pixels-trio-3-pro}. Its two-cable path needs no driver, and its one-cable path uses Mobile Pixels' driver. ChatGPT's 'premium' Xebec costs $699 plus a $59 adapter on any Mac, and its 'avoid hinge stress' ViewSonic VG1457 cannot extend both screens on macOS. Neither should be offered to a MacBook owner as a two-extra-screen answer. The Aura Dual Boost 14 ($289, Aura US store) also needs a driver, so it uses the same driver path as the FOPO S788. For one added screen, the Duex Max DS is {after:mobile-pixels-duex-max-ds} through our link, against the $299.99 card ChatGPT showed (seller not named).
